study_notes.topic: Classification or Odd One Out (Verbal Reasoning)

sections.title: Level 2 Classification Strategy
sections.content: At Level 2, the pattern becomes slightly more complex. Step 1: Observe all the options carefully. Step 2: Identify the relationship or pattern among each option. Step 3: Apply mathematical, linguistic, or logical rules. Step 4: The option that does not follow the same rule will be the Odd One Out.

sections.title: Word Pair Classification
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the relationship between the given words. Step 2: Check whether the relationship relates to category, profession, place, or function. Step 3: Verify that the same relationship exists in all pairs. Step 4: The pair that does not follow the same relationship will be the Odd One Out. Example: Tabla : Musician, Brush : Painter, Stethoscope : Doctor, Book : Reader. Here Book : Reader is different because the other three pairs show an instrument or tool related to a profession.

sections.title: Number Cluster Classification
sections.content: Step 1: Find the relationship among numbers such as square, cube, or multiplication. Step 2: Check whether the square or cube of a number is related to the next number. Step 3: Examine digit sum, factors, or power relationships. Step 4: The cluster that does not follow the same mathematical rule will be the Odd One Out. Example: (3, 9, 27), (4, 16, 64), (5, 25, 125), (6, 36, 200). The last cluster is different because the cube of 6 is 216, not 200.

sections.title: Letter Cluster Classification
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the alphabetical positions of the letters. Step 2: Check whether the shift is forward or backward. Step 3: Observe vowel and consonant alternating patterns. Step 4: Also examine reverse alphabetical logic (A=26, B=25). Example: BDF, HJL, NPR, TVY. Here TVY is different because the others follow a +2 alphabetical gap.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Looking at word pair relationships only superficially. 2. Checking only one mathematical operation in number clusters. 3. Ignoring forward and reverse alphabetical shifts. 4. Selecting an answer without confirming the pattern.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2 classification, identifying deeper patterns is important. In word pairs, observe analogical relationships; in number clusters, apply multi-step mathematical logic; and in letter clusters, detect complex alphabetical shifts or patterns.

tricks.title: Relationship Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: In word pairs, first understand the relationship between the two words.
tricks.example: Doctor : Hospital, Teacher : School, Pilot : Airport, Chef : Kitchen → All represent profession and workplace.

tricks.title: Function-Based Comparison
tricks.explanation: Check whether the first word uses or is associated with the second.

tricks.title: Square-Cube Check
tricks.explanation: In number clusters, see whether the square or cube of a number is related to the next number.

tricks.title: Digit Sum Logic
tricks.explanation: Sometimes the digit sum forms a pattern.

tricks.title: Prime Factor Check
tricks.explanation: Prime factors of numbers may also form a pattern.

tricks.title: Forward and Backward Alphabet Check
tricks.explanation: Check alphabetical shifts in both forward and backward directions.

tricks.title: Vowel-Consonant Alternation
tricks.explanation: Some clusters follow alternating vowel and consonant patterns.
tricks.example: A, B, E, F, I, J.

tricks.title: Reverse Alphabet Method
tricks.explanation: Also check reverse alphabetical values (A=26, B=25).
